title: 34 Airbnb Review Examples to Leave for Your Host (2026)
summary: 34 Airbnb review examples to leave for your host, from great stays to minor snags and one-liners, plus how Airbnb's 14-day review window works.
body_markdown:
The best review for an Airbnb host names one or two concrete details a future guest can use: how check-in went, how clean the home was, or one specific note about the area or host. Stay honest and submit it within 14 days of checkout. Below are 34 copyable examples grouped by situation.


## What makes an Airbnb review useful to the next guest?


A useful Airbnb review answers the questions the next guest has before booking, and those follow Airbnb's six rating categories: cleanliness, accuracy, check-in, communication, location and value ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1257) ). Next to your review, Airbnb shows where you are from, when you stayed, your trip type (with kids, a group or pets) and how long you stayed, and guests can search reviews by keyword ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ). A review that says "wifi," "parking," "stairs" or "kids" turns up when the next guest searches for that word.


A review that covers four things is enough:


1. Who traveled and for how long, for example "two of us, four nights" or "a family with a toddler."
2. One detail about the place that a guest could check, like the desk setup or how dark the bedroom gets.
3. One fact about the host, such as how fast they answered.
4. One thing the next guest should plan around, like stairs or street parking.


Compare a weak sentence with a useful one. Weak: "Great place, clean and cozy, \[Host name\] was very nice, would stay again." Useful: "My partner and I stayed four nights; the bedroom stayed quiet even on a Saturday night, and \[Host name\] said yes to a noon checkout the same evening I asked."


## What are good review examples for a great Airbnb stay?


Good review examples for a great stay give future guests checkable facts in place of general praise. A door code that worked or wifi that held up on video calls tells the next guest what to expect, and high marks in all six categories are one of the inputs Airbnb uses for its Guest Favorite badge ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3496) ). Each of the 8 reviews below fits a different trip type and length, so pick the closest one and swap in your own details.


1. "My partner and I spent three nights here, and the self check-in door code worked on the first try. The apartment was spotless and the beach was a six-minute walk down the road. \[Host name\] sent clear parking instructions the morning we arrived."
2. "We stayed four nights with our toddler and appreciated that \[Host name\] had the travel crib and high chair set up before we walked in. The fenced backyard gave us a safe place to play, and the washer and dryer handled our laundry without a hitch. Grocery stores in \[neighborhood\] were a five-minute drive away."
3. "I booked this studio for a five-day work trip and took video calls all week from the desk by the window without a single drop. The street was quiet during daytime meetings, and the nearest train station was a seven-minute walk. \[Host name\] checked in on arrival day to confirm the keypad worked."
4. "Six of us stayed for a long weekend and had plenty of seating around the dining table and living room sofa. Both bathrooms kept steady hot water even when everyone got ready back to back. \[Host name\] left a printed guide on the counter with coffee shops and dinner spots in \[neighborhood\] that we used twice. Self check-in made life easy for the friends who landed on a later flight."
5. "I lived in this apartment for a full month and found the kitchen stocked with real cookware, sharp knives, and a full-size fridge. Trash pickup instructions were posted inside the pantry, and the bedroom closet had enough hangers and shelf space for four weeks of clothes. \[Host name\] messaged halfway through the month to offer fresh towels and linens. The quiet block in \[neighborhood\] made working and sleeping easy."
6. "We traveled with our beagle for three nights. The backyard fence had a solid latch with no gaps, and \[Host name\] left two bowls and a towel for muddy paws right by the back door. A shaded walking trail in \[neighborhood\] was ten minutes away on foot."
7. "I booked this home for a weekend with my parents in their seventies, and the layout worked well for them. The driveway led to a step-free front entrance and the main bathroom had a walk-in shower with a grab bar. Both bedrooms had firm mattresses and blackout curtains. \[Host name\] answered my questions about doorway widths before we booked."
8. "We spent five nights here for our honeymoon and drank coffee on the private balcony facing the water each morning. The house sat on a quiet lane in \[neighborhood\], yet dinner spots were still a ten-minute walk away. \[Host name\] left a handwritten welcome note and a printed list of local favorites that led us to our best meal of the trip."


## How do you review a good stay that had one problem?


A good stay with one problem is best reviewed by leading with what went right and stating the problem as a plain fact. A future guest can then judge whether it matters for their own trip, and the host reads a fair account of the stay. Each of the six versions below deals with a different problem.


1. "We would book this house again for the breakfast tips alone; \[Host name\] knows \[neighborhood\] well, and the place was very clean. One thing to note: water pressure in the upstairs shower is quite light, though the downstairs shower had strong pressure and plenty of hot water."
2. "We loved the bright living room, comfortable queen bed, and five-minute walk to restaurants in \[neighborhood\]. Because the bedroom faces a main street, traffic noise picks up around 11 pm on weekends. Bringing earplugs solved it for us, and \[Host name\] was responsive throughout our stay."
3. "Central location and very clean rooms, with easy keypad entry and fast replies from \[Host name\]. If you plan to cook full meals, bring your own staples because the kitchen had plates and two pans but no cooking oil, salt, or baking sheet. For grabbing takeout or making simple breakfasts, the setup worked fine."
4. "Everything matched the photos. Street parking in \[neighborhood\] filled up after 7 pm, so we parked two blocks away on both evenings. Arriving earlier in the afternoon or using rideshare makes things much easier."
5. "The flat was tidy and \[Host name\] answered every message the same day. Future guests should know the unit sits up three narrow flights of stairs with no elevator, which was a workout with heavy suitcases. Pack light if you book it."
6. "We spent most mornings on the porch of this quiet cottage. The wifi worked fine for email and browsing, though it lagged during video calls and dropped once during a meeting. Good for a vacation, less reliable if you need to work remotely all day."


## How do you write an honest mixed review on Airbnb?


An honest mixed review on Airbnb describes what happened and keeps the home separate from the host, because a worn apartment can come with a very responsive host. Other guests never see your individual category scores, so the written text is the only place they learn why you gave three stars. Use the five reviews below for stays that were fine in some ways and disappointing in others.


1. "\[Host name\] answered messages quickly and check-in was smooth, though the apartment felt smaller than the wide-angle listing photos suggested. The second bedroom barely fit a suitcase beside the bed, and the living room seats three comfortably rather than five. Clean space for a couple, tight for a larger group."
2. "The location in \[neighborhood\] was convenient and the beds had fresh linens, but the cleaning missed a few noticeable spots. We found heavy dust along the bedroom baseboards, pet hair on the rug, and a load of unwashed mugs still in the dishwasher. \[Host name\] apologized when we messaged, and a more thorough turnover would make this a much better stay."
3. "Once we got inside, the studio matched the photos and was quiet at night. Check-in took about 20 minutes because the arrival message left out the building number and which side door held the lockbox. \[Host name\] picked up on the second call to walk us in, though clearer written instructions would save future guests the hassle."
4. "The house was clean and well kept, and \[Host name\] was polite over chat. Reaching downtown took a 25-minute bus ride rather than the quick walk we expected from looking at the map pin, and there were few restaurants within walking distance in \[neighborhood\]. Good option if you have a car and want quiet evenings."
5. "Everything worked as described and the walk to the train was convenient, though the space felt worn for the nightly price. The sofa cushions sagged, the kitchen cabinets stuck, and two bathroom towels were frayed. \[Host name\] communicated well, so updating the furniture would bring the home closer to its rate."


## What should you write when something went wrong and the host fixed it?


A review of a stay where something broke and the host fixed it shows the next guest how that host handles trouble. Any home can have an appliance fail or a code stop working, so write down how fast the host answered and what they did. Name the problem, the response time, and the fix, as in these five.


1. "The air conditioning stopped cooling on our second afternoon during a heat wave. I messaged \[Host name\], who called an HVAC technician right away and had the unit repaired the same evening. The rest of the house was comfortable and well kept, and I would trust \[Host name\] with a future booking."
2. "Our flight landed late and the lockbox code failed when we reached the door at 11 pm. \[Host name\] answered the phone on the first ring, walked us through the backup keypad code, and checked in the next morning to make sure we settled in fine. Once inside, the apartment was clean, warm, and quiet."
3. "When we arrived for a four-person stay, there were only two bath towels in the closet. I sent a quick note and \[Host name\] dropped off a fresh stack of towels and washcloths within an hour. Everything else in the home matched the listing, and communication stayed fast all weekend."
4. "A pipe under the kitchen sink started leaking on our first night. \[Host name\] came by to shut the valve within 30 minutes and moved us to a comparable apartment two blocks away in \[neighborhood\] so we would not have to stay during repairs. The rest of our week there went smoothly."
5. "The water heater went out on Sunday morning and left us without hot water for our last day. \[Host name\] arranged a plumber right away and refunded that night's stay without us having to ask. Apart from that morning, the house was clean and close to everything we wanted to see."


## What are some short Airbnb review examples?


Short reviews are fine when you have a minute on your phone and still want to help the next guest. One sentence works if it carries a fact a future guest can use. All 10 one-liners below are under 20 words.


1. "Keypad check-in worked right away, and \[Host name\] replied within minutes whenever I asked a question."
2. "Comfortable queen bed, quiet street in \[neighborhood\], and a five-minute walk to the subway station."
3. "Washer and dryer in the unit saved our week; detergent pods were already under the sink."
4. "Free driveway parking for two cars, which is rare in \[neighborhood\]."
5. "Blackout curtains in both bedrooms, so the kids slept past sunrise."
6. "Bikes in the garage were free to use and the bike path starts at the end of the street."
7. "Clean rooms and accurate photos, with a grocery store two blocks away."
8. "The rooftop terrace gets afternoon sun and has seating for six."
9. "Ten minutes from the airport, so our 6 a.m. flight was no stress."
10. "Smooth self check-in at midnight and clear checkout notes waiting on the kitchen counter."


## How does Airbnb's review system work for guests?


Airbnb's review system prompts guests and hosts on checkout day and gives both sides 14 days after checkout to write a review ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ). Neither side can read the other's review until both are in or the 14 days run out, whichever comes first, so a guest can be honest without worrying about what the host writes back about them. After day 14 Airbnb makes no exceptions for late reviews; it suggests sending the host a message instead ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/995) ).


If you submit your review first, you can edit it at any time during the 14-day window until the host submits theirs; once a review is published, no changes are allowed ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/367) ). You can remove a review you wrote up to 30 days after publication ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3582) ), though once it is removed you cannot write a new review for that reservation ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) ).


Airbnb asks for your overall star rating as its own question and does not calculate it from the six category scores ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1257) ). Giving 4 or 5 stars in a category lets you pick tags such as "Easy to find" or "Personal welcome," and lower ratings offer tags like "Hard to locate" or "Unclear instructions." The cleanliness question asks whether the home was free of mold and pests and of extensive dust, pet dander and dirty dishes (same page). Your overall rating matters to the host: Superhost status needs a 4.8 or higher average ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/829) ), and Airbnb describes Guest Favorites as averaging above 4.9 stars ([Airbnb Resource Center](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/why-reviews-matter-41) ). A 4-star overall score for a stay you liked pulls the host's average toward that 4.8 line, so give the overall score you mean.


## Which parts of your Airbnb review can the public see?


Anyone browsing Airbnb can read your written review, your overall star rating and some trip context, while your individual category scores and your note to the host are visible only to the host and Airbnb ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ). Airbnb says it may still use any review information, notes included, for Guest Favorites and search results. The table shows who sees each part.


Part of the review Who can see it


Written public review Public on the listing, host, and Airbnb


Overall star rating Public next to your review; the listing's average shows once it has 3 reviews ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1257) )


Your six category ratings Your individual scores: host and Airbnb only; each category's average across all reviews is public


Note to the host Host and Airbnb only


Your city/country, trip type, length of stay Public next to your review (unless you opt out), host, and Airbnb


The note to the host is the right place for small fixes, such as a sticky lock or a burnt-out bulb, that the next guest does not need to read about.


## What will Airbnb remove from a review?


Airbnb takes down reviews that break its[Reviews Policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) or[Content Policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/546) , including irrelevant, fake, incentivized, retaliatory, or privacy-violating posts. Reviews count as irrelevant when the guest never arrived or cancelled for reasons unrelated to the home. Airbnb also prohibits trading or withholding a review for something of value, such as a discount, a refund, or a reciprocal positive review, as well as reviews written to harm competition.


Content Policy removals cover harassment, discrimination, and publicly sharing another person's private information, including details sufficient to identify a listing's exact location, and the same rules apply to AI-generated content ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/546) ). Do not include the door code, street address, or the host's phone number anywhere in a public review. Airbnb keeps reviews up when the host only disagrees with the star rating, and it treats opinions ("the kitchen was small") and things outside the host's control, such as a noisy neighborhood, as fair comment ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) ).


## How should a host reply to these reviews?


Hosts on Airbnb can post a public reply to a guest review, and the reply appears under the review as soon as it is submitted ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/32) ). Future guests read replies to see how a host handles feedback, so thank the guest, keep it short and name any fix you made, such as a new line on your[Airbnb cleaning checklist](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/the-ultimate-airbnb-cleaning-checklist-for-hosts) . For the reviews you write about guests, use the[Airbnb guest review templates](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/20-airbnb-host-review-templates-and-automated-workflows) .


1. Reply to a 5-star review: "Thanks for staying with us, \[Guest name\]. Glad the keypad check-in was smooth and the workspace held up for your calls. You are welcome back anytime."
2. Reply to a one-problem review: "Thanks for the honest feedback, \[Guest name\]. Glad the apartment worked well for your trip, and thank you for flagging the upstairs shower pressure. Our plumber replaced the showerhead yesterday so it is back to full strength."
3. Reply to a mixed review: "Thank you for sharing the details of your stay, \[Guest name\]. I am sorry the arrival instructions were unclear and that our cleaners missed the baseboards. We added the building number to our check-in message and reviewed the turnover steps with our cleaning team."

## FAQ


Airbnb's review rules change with the type of booking and with what happened to the reservation. A home stay gives you 14 days to review, an Experience gives you 30, and a trip cancelled before check-in day cannot be reviewed at all. If you are unsure whether a review is still open, check whether the stay is listed under Reviews to write in your profile.


### How long do you have to leave an Airbnb review?


Guests have 14 days to review an Airbnb home, counted from the day of checkout ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/995) ). If the stay still shows under Reviews to write in your profile, you can review it. Once it moves to Expired reviews, Airbnb allows no late reviews, and a message to the host is the only way left to share feedback.


### Can the host see my review before I write mine?


A host cannot read your review before writing theirs. Airbnb holds both reviews and publishes them together once both are in or the 14-day window closes ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ). The rule works both ways, so you also cannot read what the host wrote about you before you submit your own.


### Do Airbnb Experience reviews work the same way?


Airbnb Experience and service reviews work differently from home reviews: you get 30 days instead of 14, only guests write reviews, and a review is published as soon as you submit it ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/995) ). Hosts can still post a public response.


### Are Airbnb category star ratings public?


Your individual category ratings are visible only to the host and Airbnb ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ). Other guests see each category's average across all of the listing's reviews ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1257) ), so your scores count toward those averages without being tied to your name.


### Should I mention problems in my public review that I already told the host privately?


Mention a problem in your public review if a future guest would plan around it, such as a steep driveway or thin walls, even if you already told the host. If the host fixed it during your stay, say that too. A loose cabinet handle you reported and saw fixed does not need a public mention.


### Can I leave an Airbnb review if I cancelled or never stayed?


Reservations cancelled before check-in day cannot be reviewed. If you booked but never showed up, Airbnb treats any review as lacking first-hand experience and can remove it under its Reviews Policy ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) ). Some reservations cancelled on or after check-in day can still be reviewed ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ).
